Resonator_obs experienced a genuine transient environmental perturbation (thermal, vibrational, or electromagnetic) on day 30 that is not affecting other instruments equally; instrument sensitivity or geometry makes it selective.

Instrumental noise floor dominates all four instruments; baseline stability is an artifact of ensemble averaging independent white/red noise; day 30 resonator_obs excursion is a rare high-variance tail of the noise distribution, not signal.

Resonator_obs is being read or logged with different temporal resolution, trial binning, or averaging window than the other three instruments; day 30 represents a change in acquisition or data-handling protocol specific to resonator_obs.

Resonator_obs calibration drifted or recalibration was performed between day 10 and day 30; the baseline established on days 1–10 no longer reflects the true zero/reference for post-baseline trials, and day 30 reflects incipient re-zeroing or instrumental instability.

A colleague or external measurement at resonator_obs location on day 30 introduced a brief disturbance (vibration, thermal shock, or electromagnetic interference) that I am not aware of; operator error or unlogged maintenance.
Residual: Unidentified systematic error or measurement artifact I have not yet conceived; possible misdating of day 30 events, data-entry corruption, or a real but exotic physical phenomenon.

Resonator_obs experienced a genuine transient environmental perturbation (thermal, vibrational, or electromagnetic) on day 40 that is not affecting other instruments equally; instrument sensitivity or geometry makes it selective.

Instrumental noise floor dominates all four instruments; the day 30 and day 40 resonator_obs excursions are rare high-variance tails of the noise distribution, not signal. The earlier probability of this hypothesis was weakened by day 30 data; day 40 now further weakens it because identical behavior recurred.

Resonator_obs is being read or logged with different temporal resolution, trial binning, or averaging window than the other three instruments on specific days (e.g., day 30, day 40); protocol changes or sensor acquisition drift specific to resonator_obs.

Resonator_obs calibration drifted or was intermittently corrupted between baseline (days 1–10) and day 40; the zero-point or reference is no longer reliable, and days 30 and 40 reflect degradation thresholds or re-zeroing attempts.

A human or environmental event at the resonator_obs location on day 40 (and separately, on day 30) introduced a brief, localized disturbance (vibration, thermal shock, electromagnetic interference, or unlogged maintenance) that I am not aware of; operator error or unplanned activity.

Residual: unidentified systematic error, measurement artifact, or exotic physical phenomenon. Possible explanations include data-entry corruption specific to resonator_obs on days 30 and 40, a real but unanticipated coupling between resonator_obs and an environmental cycle (e.g., settlement power load, outdoor thermal cycle, or equipment startup), or a true instrumental pathology I have not yet conceived.
